page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is a virtual server powered by a 16-core Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a sustained 3.1 GHz clock speed on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 32 vCPUs via 2-way hyper-threading and 128 GB of dedicated RAM, establishing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware features include AVX-512 instruction set extensions with Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), AES encryption support, and 35 MB of L3 cache. The instance contains no bundled local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on remote storage volumes and a 10 Gbps baseline network connection.

In performance evaluations, the instance records middle-tier compute and memory bandwidth results. Benchmarks demonstrate a multi-core stress-ng CPU score of 30666.35 and a total PassMark CPU rating of 29517.51. Uncached memory throughput reaches 109.89 GB/sec for read operations and 48.22 GB/sec for write operations. Application testing yields 28.91 million operations per second for Redis SET workloads, a software compilation score of 23704 in Geekbench, and CPU-based LLM inference rates of 12.4 tokens/sec for 7B parameter text generation.

The instance offers a predictable cost profile by eliminating GPU and local NVMe storage overhead while providing dedicated CPU core allocations. However, reliance on network-attached storage introduces I/O latency considerations for storage-bound applications. The resource profile supports general-purpose backend services, microservices architectures, continuous integration software compilation, medium-scale caching layers, and web application hosting.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 vCPUs and 16 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores operating at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 128 GB of system RAM, it maintains a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio alongside hardware support for AVX-512 VNNI instructions. The server lacks bundled local disk storage or GPU accelerators, using network storage backed by 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. In synthetic benchmarks, the machine achieves average performance, registering a PassMark CPU score of 29517.51 and uncached read memory bandwidth of 109.89 GB/sec. Workload benchmarks show 28.91 million operations per second in Redis SET testing and 12.4 tokens per second during CPU-based 7B model LLM text generation. The configuration provides steady compute density suitable for web serving, microservices, build compilation, and backend application processing.
